subject: Estimating abundance in multisession SECR using region.N

messages.author: 1661308b34ed6271
messages.subject: Estimating abundance in multisession SECR using region.N
parts:
Hi all,

I have a multi-site SECR model that I am using to estimate snow leopard population densities and abundance. I am using the best fit spatial covariate model for reporting densities and abundances.

When I try to use the region.N function to estimate abundance from this multi-site model, I get this error:

region.N(best_mod, covmask.list, pooled.RN = TRUE)
Error in sumDpdot(object, sessnum, regionmask, D, noneuc, cellsize, constant = FALSE,  :
  dims [product 27300] do not match the length of object [33720]

## Removing the pooled.RN argument gives me estimates for each session.
region.N(best_mod, covmask.list)
[[1]]
    estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl n
E.N 20.84802    3.724021 14.73023 29.50666 2
R.N 18.70105         NaN      NaN      NaN 2

[[2]]
    estimate SE.estimate     lcl      ucl n
E.N 16.90213    3.290729 11.5813 24.66752 1
R.N 15.79853         NaN     NaN      NaN 1

[[3]] and so on.....

What is the best way to estimate abundance for the entire region of interest?

Many thanks,
Manvi

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Estimating abundance in multisession SECR using region.N
parts:
I can't tell whether this is a limitation in 'secr' or an error in your setup. 'abundance' as you use the term is generally a nonsense parameter, especially with spatial covariate models that extrapolate outside the immediate area of the detectors.
Murray
